facts.statement: Barinasuchus was described by Paolillo and Linares in 2007.
facts.quote: authority: Paolillo and Linares, 2007

facts.statement: Barinasuchus is an extinct genus of sebecid mesoeucrocodylian.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus (meaning "Barinas crocodile", in reference to where the type material was found) is an extinct genus of sebecid mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus lived in Argentina, Peru, and Venezuela from the middle Eocene to the Late Miocene, approximately 42 to 11.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived in Argentina, Peru, and Venezuela between the middle Eocene and the Late Miocene, ~42–11.6 Ma.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered by road workers in Venezuela in 1973 but was largely destroyed during excavation, leaving only a partial snout and mandible.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Barinasuchus, discovered by road workers in Venezuela in 1973, originally consisted of a substantial portion of the skeleton, though much of it was accidentally destroyed when they attempted to excavate it, leaving only a partial snout and mandible (lower jaw).

facts.statement: The type specimen comes from the Miocene-age Parángula Formation.
facts.quote: The specimen comes from the Miocene-age Parángula Formation

facts.statement: A second specimen from the Miocene Ipururo Formation of Peru was originally described in 1977 as Sebecus huilensis but is now considered Langstonia.
facts.quote: A second specimen of Barinasuchus was recovered from the Miocene Ipururo Formation of Peru, and was described in 1977 by Éric Buffetaut and Robert Hoffstetter, though was originally assigned to Sebecus huilensis (now Langstonia).

facts.statement: A third specimen was recovered in 1984 from the Eocene-age Divisadero Largo Formation of Argentina.
facts.quote: Another was recovered from the Eocene-age Divisadero Largo Formation of Argentina in 1984 by Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus was heterodont, possessing two types of teeth.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus was heterodont, meaning that it possessed two types of teeth.

facts.statement: The teeth of the premaxilla and front maxilla were longer and more conical than the shorter, thinner teeth further back.
facts.quote: Those of the premaxilla and the front of the maxilla were longer and more conical than those further back, which were shorter and thinner.

facts.statement: The mandible was very robust compared to other sebecids and widest at the fourth mandibular tooth.
facts.quote: Its mandible was very robust in comparison to other sebecids, and was widest at the point of the fourth mandibular (lower jaw) tooth.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus primarily inhabited lacustrine environments.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus primarily inhabited lacustrine (lake/lakeside) environments.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus was among the last and largest sebecids, outlasting others like Dentaneosuchus, possibly due to isolation.
facts.quote: Both were among the last and largest of the sebecids, and significantly outlasted other giant taxa, such as the European Dentaneosuchus, possibly due to their isolation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the extinction of Barinasuchus resulted from the loss of the Pebas Mega-Wetland or the diversification of mammalian predators and phorusrhacid birds.
facts.quote: The extinction of Barinasuchus and other parts of this reptile-heavy guild may have been the result of the loss of the Pebas Mega-Wetland, or the diversification of mammalian predators and the phorusrhacid birds, although this has been questioned by some studies.

facts.statement: Road workers near Qedabra Socó, Venezuela, discovered a large sebecid skeleton in 1973 while building a road to El Toro.
facts.quote: In 1973, road workers near Qedabra Socó, a tributary of the Rio Masparro river in Venezuela, near the eastern foothills of the Andes, discovered what was apparently a near-complete skeleton of a large sebecid while constructing an access road to the town of El Toro.

facts.statement: Only the anterior half of a skull and mandible remained after excavation damage, having been relocated to an institution in Barinas.
facts.quote: Only a few fragments remained at the site when it was inspected by archaeologists. What remained of the specimen, the anterior (front) half of a skull and mandible, had been removed prior to their arrival, but had fortunately been relocated to an institution, the in Barinas, by an unknown party.

facts.statement: A sebecid specimen from the middle Miocene Ipururo Formation of Peru was published by Buffetaut and Hoffstetter in 1977.
facts.quote: In 1977, Éric Buffetaut and Robert Hoffstetter published on a sebecid specimen recovered from the Ipururo Formation of eastern Peru, dated to the middle Miocene.

facts.statement: Paolillo and Linares described MAAT-0260 as Barinasuchus arveloi in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, as part of a paper describing multiple genera of South American sebecids, Alfredo Paolillo and Omar J. Linares described MAAT-0260, and assigned it to a taxon of its own, Barinasuchus arveloi.

facts.statement: The specimen described by Buffetaut and Hoffstetter was later assigned to Barinasuchus.
facts.quote: Buffetaut and Hoffstetter's specimen was assigned to the same taxon.

facts.statement: The name Barinasuchus arveloi refers to the state of Barinas and Alberto Arvelo Torrealba, namesake of the museum housing the holotype.
facts.quote: The binomial name refers to Barinas, the Venezuelan state from which the holotype is known, and to Alberto Arvelo Torrealba, a local educator and poet, the namesake of the museum where it is housed.

facts.statement: A fragmentary specimen collected by Dr. Edgardo Rolleri was assigned to Sebecosuchia indet. by Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini in 1984.
facts.quote: The second was a fragmentary specimen (M.L.P. 73-III-15-1), collected by Dr. Edgardo Rolleri and assigned to Sebecosuchia indet. by Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini in 1984.

facts.statement: The specimen collected by Rolleri comes from middle Eocene-age strata of Argentina's Divisadero Largo Formation.
facts.quote: Whereas the other two specimens were Miocene, this one comes from middle Eocene-age strata of Argentina's Divisadero Largo Formation.

facts.statement: The specimen M.L.P. 73-III-15-1 was previously tentatively assigned to Bretesuchus in a dissertation.
facts.quote: M.L.P. 73-III-15-1 had, in a dissertation, previously been tentatively assigned to Bretesuchus.

facts.statement: Due to the destruction of the holotype, the postcranial skeleton and much of the skull of Barinasuchus are unknown.
facts.quote: Due to the near-total destruction of the holotype, the postcranial skeleton of Barinasuchus (the elements behind the skull) are unknown, and much of the skull is also absent.

facts.statement: Molnar and Mequita de Vasconcellos used anatomical proxies to estimate Barinasuchus size in 2016.
facts.quote: In 2016, Ralph E. Molnar and Felipe Mequita de Vasconcellos used several anatomical proxies in an attempt to determine its size.

facts.statement: Molnar and Mequita de Vasconcellos used the baurusuchid genus Stratiotosuchus as a reference for size estimation.
facts.quote: Firstly, they used another sebecosuchian, the baurusuchid genus Stratiotosuchus, as a frame of reference, due to its completeness.

facts.statement: Using Stratiotosuchus as a reference, Molnar and Mequita de Vasconcellos estimated a length of 6.3 m.
facts.quote: In doing so, they arrived at a length estimate of 6.3 m.

facts.statement: Using American and saltwater crocodiles as references, they estimated a length of about 7.5 m.
facts.quote: Using modern crocodilians, specifically the American and saltwater crocodiles, as reference points, they attained a larger estimate of about 7.5 m.

facts.statement: Based on head-length ratios, they suggested a maximum body length of 10 m.
facts.quote: Based on the variability of head-length-to-total-length ratios in modern taxa, they suggested that Barinasuchus may have attained a maximum body length of 10 m.

facts.statement: They provided a body mass estimate of 1,610–1,720 kg.
facts.quote: For body mass, they provided an estimate of 1,610–1,720 kg.

facts.statement: With a 50% margin of error, the estimated mass would exceed that of any extant terrestrial predatory mammal and equal that of a black rhinoceros.
facts.quote: Even taking a margin of error of 50% into account, this would make Barinasuchus heavier than any (extant) terrestrial predatory mammal, and is roughly equal in mass to a black rhinoceros.

facts.statement: Subsequent papers proposed considerably smaller sizes for Barinasuchus.
facts.quote: However, considerably smaller sizes, both in terms of body length and body mass, were proposed by subsequent papers.

facts.statement: A 2023 paper suggested that Barinasuchus was around 3–4 m in length.
facts.quote: The 2023 paper describing Dentaneosuchus, for example, suggested that both it and Barinasuchus were somewhere around 3–4 m in length.

facts.statement: A 2025 paper by Bravo et al. calculated a mean body mass of 500 kg, with other estimates ranging from 179–1,388 kg.
facts.quote: Similarly, in the supplementary materials of a paper published in 2025, Gonzalo Gabriel Bravo and colleagues calculated a considerably lighter mean body mass of 500 kg accounting for a very large margin of error; estimates otherwise ranged from 179–1,388 kg.

facts.statement: Based on preserved dimensions, the total skull length of Barinasuchus is estimated to be about 1 meter.
facts.quote: Based on these dimensions, Barinasuchus likely had a total skull length of about 1 m.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus possesses the largest skull of any known sebecosuchian, while Bretesuchus has the second largest at 66 cm.
facts.quote: This would make it the largest skull of any sebecosuchian; that of Bretesuchus was the second largest, measuring 66 cm as preserved.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus had a tall and laterally compressed rostrum, a condition known as oreinirostral in crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: Its rostrum was tall and laterally compressed, a condition which, in crocodyliforms, is referred to as being oreinirostral.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Barinasuchus are curved to form a narrow dome shape.
facts.quote: The nasals are curved, forming a narrow dome shape.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus had a perinarial fossa that was slightly larger than in other sebecids, similar to Ogresuchus and Sebecus.
facts.quote: Like Ogresuchus and Sebecus, the perinarial fossa (a depression on the lower margin of the nasal opening) was slightly larger than in other sebecids.

facts.statement: The fourth mandibular tooth of Barinasuchus was the largest tooth in both jaws and was curved.
facts.quote: The fourth mandibular tooth was the largest (out of both upper and lower jaws), and was curved.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus had heterodont dentition, meaning it possessed multiple different tooth shapes.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus dentition was heterodont, meaning that multiple tooth morphologies were present.

facts.statement: A 2025 analysis by Bravo et al. recovered Barinasuchus as the sister taxon to a clade containing the Lumbrera form and Sebecus species.
facts.quote: In 2025, Gonzalo Gabriel Bravo and colleagues recovered Barinasuchus as the sister taxon to a clade consisting entirely of the Lumbrera form and Sebecus species.

facts.statement: Later specimens of Barinasuchus lived up to the middle Miocene in a northern South American ecosystem dominated by non-mammalian predators.
facts.quote: Up to around the middle Miocene, when the later specimens of Barinasuchus lived, the northern South American predatory guild was mostly non-mammalian, with many constituent taxa being reptiles and especially archosaurs.

facts.statement: Langstonia was contemporaneous with Barinasuchus and lived in South America.
facts.quote: Only three definite sebecosuchians of similar size are known: one, Dentaneosuchus, lived in Europe and became extinct in the Eocene; the second, Bretesuchus, was also South American and lived during the Palaeocene; the third, Langstonia, was contemporaneous with Barinasuchus and also lived in South America.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus inhabited the Pebas Mega-Wetland and adjacent regions during the Miocene.
facts.quote: It is the Pebas Mega-Wetland and adjacent regions which Barinasuchus would have inhabited, at least during the Miocene.

facts.statement: The holotype of Barinasuchus was recovered from the upper part of the Parángula Formation, dating to the lower middle Miocene.
facts.quote: The holotype of Barinasuchus was recovered from strata belonging to the upper part of the Parángula Formation, dating to the lower middle Miocene.

facts.statement: The earliest known specimen of Barinasuchus comes from the mid-Eocene Divisadero Largo Formation, deposited in a shallow lacustrine environment.
facts.quote: The mid-Eocene Divisadero Largo Formation, from which the earliest Barinasuchus specimen is known, was similarly deposited in a shallow lacustrine environment.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus and other similarly sized sebecosuchians appear to have been apex predators.
facts.quote: All of these taxa appear to have been apex predators.

facts.statement: Barinasuchus was described in 2007 by Alfredo Paolillo and Omar Linares.
facts.quote: Barinasuchus fue descrito en 2007 por Alfredo Paolillo y Omar Linares.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an incomplete articulated frontal skull and lower jaw from the Parangula Formation in Barinas, Venezuela.
facts.quote: El holotipo proviene de rocas de la formación Parángula en Barinas, Venezuela y consiste de la parte frontal del cráneo incompleto articulado y la mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: A specimen from Peru was originally described as Sebecus huilensis in 1977 before being reassigned to Barinasuchus.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen de Perú fue descrito como Sebecus huilensis en 1977, antes de ser referido a Barinasuchus.

facts.statement: Fossils have been found in the Middle Eocene Divisadero Largo Formation of Argentina (tentatively assigned) and in the Middle Miocene Ipururo Formation of Peru and Parangula Formation of Venezuela.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles han sido hallados en rocas del Eoceno medio de la Formación Divisadero Largo de Argentina (asignados de manera tentativa), y en la formación Ipururo de Perú y la formación Parángula de Venezuela, ambas de mediados del Mioceno.

facts.statement: The genus lived from the Lutetian to the Tortonian stages, between 42 and 11 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Tortonian (42 to 11 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other sebecosuchians, it was a terrestrial carnivore with teeth resembling those of theropod dinosaurs rather than modern crocodilians, which were laterally compressed and had serrated edges.
facts.quote: Como otros sebecosuquios, era un carnívoro terrestre dotado con dientes más parecidos a los de los dinosaurios terópodos que a los de los cocodrilianos actuales, estos eran comprimidos lateralmente y tenían bordes aserrados.

facts.statement: The preserved part of the skull is 70 cm long and 40 cm high, with an estimated total skull length of 95 to 110 cm.
facts.quote: La parte preservada del cráneo tiene 70 centímetros de largo y 40 centímetros de alto; se estima que la longitud total del cráneo es de 95-110 centímetros.

facts.statement: The total length of the animal is estimated at nearly 6 meters based on comparisons with more complete sebecosuchians like Stratiotosuchus, making it the largest known sebecid.
facts.quote: La longitud total del animal se estima en casi 6 metros basándose en la comparación con sebecosuquios más completos como Stratiotosuchus, lo que lo convierte en el mayor sebécido conocido.

facts.statement: Estimates based on the lengths of Stratiotosuchus maxhechti and Crocodylus porosus indicate masses of 1,610 and 1,720 kilograms, respectively.
facts.quote: las estimaciones basadas en las longitudes de Stratiotosuchus maxhechti y Crocodylus porosus, indican masas de 1,610 y 1,720 kilogramos respectivamente

facts.statement: Barinasuchus belongs to the family Sebecidae.
facts.quote: familia: Sebecidae

facts.statement: The genus authority is Paolillo & Linares, 2007.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Paolillo & Linares, 2007

facts.statement: The type species is B. arveloi, described by Paolillo & Linares in 2007.
facts.quote: subdivision: *B. arveloi Paolillo & Linares, 2007 (especie tipo)

facts.statement: In a cladogram, Barinasuchus is classified as a Sebecosuchian of the family Sebecidae, closely related to the genus Lorosuchus and forming the sister taxon to the genera Ayllusuchus and Bretesuchus, indicating it represents a fairly basal lineage within the family.
facts.quote: En su cladograma, Barinasuchus está clasificado como un Sebecosuchia de la familia Sebecidae, cercano al género Lorosuchus y conformando el taxón hermano de los géneros Ayllusuchus y Bretesuchus, lo que indica que Barinasuchus representa un linaje bastante basal dentro de la familia.

facts.statement: This dentition made it a formidable predator.
facts.quote: Esta dentición lo convertía en un depredador formidable.
